note: From the OpenStreetMap export (main API, 14 October 2026; tools/osm-to-kit.mjs, with its rails and platforms) and the view from above (docs/reference/aerial/cheadle-hulme.jpg), at real scale. Positive v is east-south-east. Four platforms in a V: 1 and 2 on the Crewe line, 3 and 4 on the Macclesfield line, which joins it at Cheadle Hulme North Junction about 380 m north. Platform 1 (the halt, trains towards Manchester) is west of the Crewe line and 2 east of it, 1.68 m from its tracks where OpenStreetMap has them (towards Manchester at v -3.52, towards Crewe at 0), u -105 to 80 and -101 to 70: the halt is their north part, the extension the rest, and trains stop 15 m south of the station's point. Platforms 3 and 4 (the platforms stage) stand 1.68 m from the Macclesfield tracks as the network has them (from OpenStreetMap): 3 west of the line towards Manchester (u -84 to 68, held clear of platform 2 at the V's point), 4 east of the line towards Macclesfield (u -79 to 87); at an angle to the Crewe line, so drawn as outlines 3.5 m wide. Both lines cross Station Road (A5149) on bridges just south of the point. Photos (docs/reference/photos/cheadle-hulme: entrance-1.jpg Trevor Harris 2022; platform-1-2-1.jpg, platform-2-1.jpg, platform-2-2.jpg, platform-3-1.jpg, roadbridge-2.jpg, area-bridges-1.jpg DS Pugh 2026; roadbridge-1.jpg Gerald England 2019): one lattice footbridge over all four at u 41 (the export's path) with stairs and brick lift towers; the old brick station building on Station Road at street level between the lines (the export's outline, the booking office; its hipped roof from memory); steps from Station Road up to platform 1 (the export's). Shelters, lamps, canopies, boards, shops and barriers placed by eye. No taxi rank in the photos or the export: the rank on the lane behind platform 1 is the game's. The car park is the export's public one off Station Approach (whether it is the station's is not known); the replacement bus stop on Station Road placed by eye.
